title: Switch It On with a Drug

scenes.tts: If the window waits for inhibition, what happens in a mouse that cannot release enough gaba?
scenes.caption: If the window waits for inhibition, what happens in a mouse that cannot release enough GABA?
scenes.visual: Title card: Switch It On with a Drug. An inhibitory terminal with GABA vesicles.
scenes.narration: If the window waits for inhibition, what happens in a mouse that cannot release enough GABA?

scenes.tts: Inhibitory neurons make gaba with two enzymes. One, called gad sixty-five, sits at the synaptic terminal.
scenes.caption: Inhibitory neurons make GABA with two enzymes. One, called GAD65, sits at the synaptic terminal.
scenes.visual: Two enzymes in a terminal, labelled GAD67 and GAD65; GAD65 sits at the release site.
scenes.narration: Inhibitory neurons make GABA with two enzymes. One, called GAD65, sits at the synaptic terminal.

scenes.tts: It tops up the supply when the neuron fires hard. A knockout lacks a working copy of that gene.
scenes.visual: The neuron fires a burst; GAD65 tops up the vesicles. Then GAD65 dims: knockout. Release during strong firing falls.
scenes.narration: It tops up the supply when the neuron fires hard. A knockout lacks a working copy of that gene.

scenes.tts: Pause and predict. Inhibition quiets neurons. Should a knockout's cortex shift more than normal when one eye closes?
scenes.visual: Predict card: GAD65 knockout, one eye closed at P28. More shift, the same, or less?
scenes.narration: Pause and predict. Inhibition quiets neurons. Should a knockout's cortex shift more than normal when one eye closes?

scenes.tts: It does not shift at all. Its neurons still respond to vision. What failed was the change.
scenes.visual: The knockout's index bar stays put. Its timeline has no band at all. Credit: Hensch, Fagiolini, Stryker and colleagues, 1998.
scenes.narration: It does not shift at all. Its neurons still respond to vision. What failed was the change.

scenes.tts: Now add diazepam. It binds the gaba receptor at a site between an alpha and a gamma subunit.
scenes.caption: Now add diazepam. It binds the GABA receptor at a site between an alpha and a gamma subunit.
scenes.visual: A GABA-A receptor ring of five subunits; diazepam docks between alpha and gamma, away from the GABA sites.
scenes.narration: Now add diazepam. It binds the GABA receptor at a site between an alpha and a gamma subunit.

scenes.tts: It makes the receptor respond more strongly to gaba. But it cannot open the channel alone.
scenes.caption: It makes the receptor respond more strongly to GABA. But it cannot open the channel alone.
scenes.visual: With GABA bound, the chloride current grows larger with diazepam. One frame with diazepam and no GABA: no current.
scenes.narration: It makes the receptor respond more strongly to GABA. But it cannot open the channel alone.

scenes.tts: So it amplifies the gaba the knockout still releases. Given during deprivation, it restored the shift.
scenes.caption: So it amplifies the GABA the knockout still releases. Given during deprivation, it restored the shift.
scenes.visual: Diazepam infused into the knockout's visual cortex during deprivation; the index bar now swings toward the open eye.
scenes.narration: So it amplifies the GABA the knockout still releases. Given during deprivation, it restored the shift.

scenes.tts: The drug did not shift the cortex by itself. The shift went toward the eye that stayed open.
scenes.visual: Diazepam with both eyes open, as reported: the bar does not move.
scenes.narration: The drug did not shift the cortex by itself. The shift went toward the eye that stayed open.

scenes.tts: Inhibition is permissive. The difference between the eyes is instructive.
scenes.visual: A gate labelled inhibition: permissive. Arrows from the eyes: instructive, choosing the direction.
scenes.narration: Inhibition is permissive. The difference between the eyes is instructive.

scenes.tts: Pause and predict. Raise a knockout to day sixty, long past the normal window. Give diazepam and close one eye.
scenes.caption: Pause and predict. Raise a knockout to day 60, long past the normal window. Give diazepam and close one eye.
scenes.visual: Predict card: GAD65 knockout at P60, plus diazepam, one eye closed. Shift or not?
scenes.narration: Pause and predict. Raise a knockout to day 60, long past the normal window. Give diazepam and close one eye.

scenes.tts: It shifts. The capacity waited into adulthood. Age had not closed a window that had never opened.
scenes.visual: The knockout's timeline: a band appears at P60. Credit: Fagiolini and Hensch, 2000.
scenes.narration: It shifts. The capacity waited into adulthood. Age had not closed a window that had never opened.

scenes.tts: Give diazepam to a normal mouse at about day fifteen, before its window. It shifts early.
scenes.caption: Give diazepam to a normal mouse at about day 15, before its window. It shifts early.
scenes.visual: Normal mouse timeline: diazepam at about P15; the band jumps early.
scenes.narration: Give diazepam to a normal mouse at about day 15, before its window. It shifts early.

scenes.tts: Give a second group two days of diazepam after eye opening, then close one eye at day twenty-eight.
scenes.caption: Give a second group two days of diazepam after eye opening, then close one eye at day 28.
scenes.visual: Second timeline: two days of diazepam just after eye opening, then deprivation at P28.
scenes.narration: Give a second group two days of diazepam after eye opening, then close one eye at day 28.

scenes.tts: Much less shift is left. The window opened early and was gone by day twenty-eight.
scenes.visual: The early band ends early; at P28 there is little left. Credit: Iwai and colleagues, 2003.
scenes.narration: Much less shift is left. The window opened early and was gone by day 28.
scenes.caption: Much less shift is left. The window opened early and was gone by day 28.

scenes.tts: In knockouts, two days of diazepam near the start of deprivation switched plasticity fully on.
scenes.visual: Knockout timeline: a short diazepam bar, then a full band of plasticity.
scenes.narration: In knockouts, two days of diazepam near the start of deprivation switched plasticity fully on.

scenes.tts: So in young cortex, a brief boost of inhibition can start a window without having to stay present.
scenes.visual: A brief diazepam bar starts a band of plasticity that outlasts it; no countdown clock. Label: young cortex; drug not needed during deprivation.
scenes.narration: So in young cortex, a brief boost of inhibition can start a window without having to stay present.

scenes.tts: This should feel backward. Why would less inhibition make a cortex harder to change?
scenes.visual: Question card: less inhibition, less plasticity?
scenes.narration: This should feel backward. Why would less inhibition make a cortex harder to change?

scenes.tts: The inhibition implicated here is thought to come largely from basket cells. Their synapses cluster on the cell bodies of pyramidal neurons.
scenes.visual: Basket-cell boutons contact a pyramidal cell body and nearby dendrites; the spike starts a little way along the axon. Label: strong control over whether and when the cell fires.
scenes.narration: The inhibition implicated here is thought to come largely from basket cells. Their synapses cluster on the cell bodies of pyramidal neurons.

scenes.tts: One leading idea: maturing basket-cell inhibition sharpens when pyramidal cells fire.
scenes.visual: Spike rasters: loose, smeared firing becomes tight and well timed as inhibition matures.
scenes.narration: One leading idea: maturing basket-cell inhibition sharpens when pyramidal cells fire.

scenes.tts: That could let the circuit tell which eye reliably drives each cell.
scenes.visual: Two eye inputs arrive; with sharp timing they are told apart, and the closed eye's input weakens.
scenes.narration: That could let the circuit tell which eye reliably drives each cell.

scenes.tts: This is a hypothesis, not a settled mechanism. The experiments establish the order: inhibition first, then plasticity.
scenes.visual: Label: hypothesis. Below it, an arrow from inhibition to plasticity.
scenes.narration: This is a hypothesis, not a settled mechanism. The experiments establish the order: inhibition first, then plasticity.

scenes.tts: Takeaway: inhibition opens the window like a trigger. The open eye still decides which way the cortex shifts.
scenes.visual: Closing card: inhibition triggers and permits; the open eye instructs.
scenes.narration: Takeaway: inhibition opens the window like a trigger. The open eye still decides which way the cortex shifts.
